text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Transport minister says a new terminal for international flights will be built at Istanbul airport by 1999.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller says $10 billion will be raised by privatisation next year.
- Iraqi Kurdish leader Jalal Talabani sees federation as the best solution for peace in northern Iraq.
- International Monetary Fund delegation to cut short their visit to Turkey due to negative attitudes of Islamist wing in the government.
- Ciller becomimg "Islamicised" since forming coalition with Islamists. She wore a headscarve at an Islamic summit in Istanbul and has started quoting the Koran in her speeches.
- Top Turkish writer Yasar Kemal, punished in Turkey under freedom of expression laws, wins award in Europe.
- Long queues of tankers form at Atas refinery after it stopped production.
- Islamists attacked press members in a social event held by youth organisation affiliated to the Welfare Party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
- Far-leftist armed group carries out organised executions of inmates who cooperated with authorities. Two prisoners have been killed by the organisation since Sunday.
